fullPassage: Emotions can be used to refer to the unconscious, neurobiological response, while feelings are the cognitive assignments we make to those emotions. This is undoubtedly a much more complicated dynamic and there is a great degree of highly detailed information explaining the interworking of these two. However, the most noteworthy application of the distinction between emotion and feeling is that human beings have some ability to cognitively assign, that is, to think about and make a decision about, just what a given emotion we experience might mean. This can be more easily grasped when thinking about a more concrete exemplar — ancient war drums. Most would agree that hearing a beating war drum does not lead one to pick a side in a given conflict. A beating war drum merely helps one march more energetically on whichever side was chosen to begin with. The neurobiological experience set off by the auditory sensation of the drums causes one to "feel" more energy toward a given end and step more quickly. Perhaps Shakespeare knew something of this when he wrote Timon's words, "follow thy drum ...".

det.korean: ③ fundamentally(근본적으로) → merely(단지): 전쟁 북은 '단지(merely)' 행진을 돕는 것이라는 원문인데, fundamentally(근본적으로)는 북이 근본적으로 행동을 변화시킨다는 뜻이 되어 문맥에 부적절

❌ ③ fundamentally → merely: 'A beating war drum fundamentally helps one march'에서 원문은 '단지(merely)' 도움을 줄 뿐이라는 제한적 의미. fundamentally(근본적으로)는 북이 근본적 변화를 일으킨다는 뜻이 되어 문맥에 부적절 ←정답
✅ ④ quickly(빠르게): 더 빠르게 발걸음을 옮긴다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 'merely'는 '단지, 그저'라는 의미로 범위를 제한합니다. 전쟁 북은 진영 선택에 영향을 주지 않고, '단지(merely)' 행진을 돕는 것뿐입니다.

det.analysis: 전치사 on + 복합관계형용사 whichever(어느 ~이든) + 명사 side(진영) + 조동사 was + 과거분사 chosen(선택된) + to부정사 to + 동사 begin(시작하다) + 전치사 with. 조건의 모든 단어(begin, chosen, on, side, to, was, whichever, with) 포함. 8단어 부합. 원문 표현 그대로.
det.tip: 'whichever side was chosen to begin with'는 '어느 진영이 처음에 선택되었든 간에'라는 양보 표현입니다. 'to begin with'는 '처음에, 애당초'라는 숙어입니다.
